Apple's annual September iPhone launch event is still about two months away, but this year will be a little different. In September, Apple will not unveil the entire iPhone lineup at once — only the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a brand-new foldable iPhone will make their debut first. Here's why.

The iPhone lineup is getting bigger

Over the past few years, the annual iPhone lineup has gradually expanded. Not long ago, only three new models were released each year: the iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, and iPhone 11 Pro Max. In 2020, with the addition of the iPhone 12 mini, the number of models launched in a year grew to four; by 2022, the iPhone 12 mini was replaced by the iPhone 14 Plus, which was later succeeded by the iPhone Air.

With the arrival of the iPhone 16e, the number of models released each year has further increased to five. Once the iPhone Ultra debuts, the annual iPhone lineup will grow to six models. That's a lot of models — if they were all launched at once, the stage would be awfully crowded.

So Apple has decided to adopt a staggered release strategy instead.

Two iPhone launches: fall and spring

The iPhone 18 lineup will include six models: iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and iPhone Ultra.

The logic behind this staggered approach is clear: flagship models in the fall, mid- and lower-tier models in the spring. Here's the breakdown:

  • Fall 2026: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Ultra
  • Spring 2027: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2

When the iPhone lineup expanded to four models, the fourth model always had disappointing launch sales — whether it was the iPhone mini or the iPhone Plus. So Apple feels it's reasonable to clearly split the lineup, giving the extra models their own dedicated moment in the spotlight.

But when it comes to the iPhone 18, things will shift slightly. Reports indicate Apple is working to unify the production processes for the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, so the differences between the two phones may be narrowed significantly.

It's still unclear whether this will result in major upgrades for the iPhone 18e or downgrades for the iPhone 18 — but the distinctions between the two phones may ultimately come down to small details like the display panel and camera.

Summary

In summary, assuming the iPhone Air doesn't ultimately get killed off (which I certainly hope won't happen) — this will be the new shape of the iPhone lineup going forward. Three models in the fall, three more in the spring. The end goal is to allow Apple to better space out its launches and get products into the hands of the right consumers.

Another possible outcome is that the average selling price of iPhones will rise, because anyone wanting to ride the wave of new hardware will have no choice but to buy the iPhone 18 Pro rather than a cheaper model.

Whether splitting the lineup will actually drive sales for all models remains to be seen, but this is the initial idea.

What are your thoughts on Apple staggering the iPhone releases? Will you pick up a new iPhone in the fall or wait until spring? Share your opinions in the comments.
